Generalizes beyond the example: applicability.goal_shape and use_when/avoid_when restate the move for any relation between two transition systems (refinement/simulation/bisimulation) too hard to show pointwise, scoped honestly to invariant-guarded forward simulation rather than all 'suffices' uses; intent frames it as backward application of two library rules making premises into children. When-not-to-use is honest and specific (no invariant that actually weakens the simulation; invariants that depend on each other; goal already as easy; README adds: invariant must stay in scope across every transition case). Consequences are specific with a real failure mode (invariant too weak => fw_sim_A_H unprovable, too strong => invariant lemmas unprovable) and name the concrete leak (concrete side must carry ex_abs einvs, Refine.thy 560-570), all consistent with the shown LI/L_invariantI code. It says what makes the leaves good for a bounded prover: each child's statement is self-contained (an invariant |= or LI), closes on its own from earlier/imported lemmas never a sibling, and the three children are independent so parallelisable.
